JOHN WICK (2014)
DETAILED SCREENPLAY-STYLE RETELLING
ORIGINAL RETELLING — NOT THE ORIGINAL SCREENPLAY

NOTE: This is an original, scene-oriented retelling of the film's story. It does not reproduce the copyrighted screenplay or dialogue.

========================================
ACT I — WHAT'S LEFT
========================================

FADE IN:

INT. WICK HOME — DAY

JOHN WICK sits alone with his grief.

His wife has recently died.

A package arrives, sent by her before she passed.

Inside is a puppy, and a note asking him to let himself feel something again.

INT. WICK HOME — LATER

Wick and the puppy begin an uneasy companionship.

For the first time in the film, there is a flicker of ordinary life.

EXT. GAS STATION — DAY

A young man named IOSEF notices Wick's car.

He offers to buy it.

Wick refuses.

Iosef's interest does not fade.

INT. WICK HOME — NIGHT

Iosef and associates break into the house.

They beat Wick unconscious.

They kill the puppy.

They steal the car.

EXT. WICK HOME — LATER

Wick wakes among the wreckage of the life he was trying to hold onto.

Something in him shifts back into an old shape.

INT. WICK HOME — NIGHT

Wick retrieves buried equipment and materials hidden beneath his floor.

The objects suggest a life he left behind completely.

He was someone else once.

He was very good at something violent.

He gave it up for love.

Now love is gone, and so is his reason for staying retired.

CUT TO BLACK.

========================================
ACT II — THE NAME RETURNS
========================================

INT. CRIMINAL UNDERWORLD OFFICE — DAY

Iosef's father, VIGGO, learns what his son has done.

Viggo recognizes the stolen car.

He recognizes what it means.

He tells his son, with real fear, exactly whose life he has just destroyed.

Iosef does not understand yet.

Viggo does.

EXT. CITY — NIGHT

Word spreads through the underworld that Wick is active again.

Old associates react with a mixture of respect and dread.

A hidden network of hotels, currency, and rules becomes visible.

Wick moves through this world as someone who once belonged to its highest tier.

INT. HOTEL — NIGHT

Wick checks into a sanctuary reserved for people like him.

The rules of this world are absolute.

No business is conducted here.

Wick abides by them, even as he prepares for violence everywhere else.

EXT. NIGHTCLUB — NIGHT

Wick locates people connected to Iosef.

The confrontation is fast, controlled, and overwhelming.

Word reaches Viggo that his men are being systematically removed.

INT. VIGGO'S OFFICE — NIGHT

Viggo offers a bounty for Wick's death.

Assassins from across the network respond.

Wick becomes the target of an entire underworld, not just one family.

EXT. CITY STREETS — NIGHT

Wick survives wave after wave of pursuit.

Each fight reveals the precision of his former life.

He is not simply angry.

He is exact.

INT. WICK HOME (RUINS) — NIGHT

An old colleague, someone who understands what Wick lost, finds him.

She does not try to talk him out of his path.

She helps him, understanding that this is no longer about revenge for a car or a dog.

It is about the last thing connecting him to his wife.

========================================
ACT III — SETTLING THE DEBT
========================================

EXT. VIGGO'S ESTATE — NIGHT

Wick moves through the compound with total purpose.

Guards fall one after another.

The estate that once represented power becomes a place of reckoning.

INT. ESTATE — CONTINUOUS

Wick reaches Iosef.

The confrontation is brief.

It ends the way Viggo feared it would from the beginning.

EXT. ESTATE GROUNDS — NIGHT

Viggo confronts Wick directly, offering what he has left to offer.

It changes nothing.

Wick finishes what began the night his home was invaded.

EXT. CITY STREET — LATER

Wick is injured but alive.

He has no home left in the way he once had one.

He has answered for what was taken from him, though nothing is truly repaid.

INT. ANIMAL SHELTER — DAY

Wick, wounded, arrives at a shelter.

He finds another dog.

It is not a replacement for anything.

It is simply a small decision to keep living, on whatever terms are left to him.

FADE OUT.

========================================
STRUCTURAL LESSON
========================================

Grieving protagonist clinging to an ordinary remnant of a lost life
        ↓
A small act of cruelty destroys that remnant
        ↓
Buried former identity is uncovered
        ↓
Underworld recognizes the danger of what has been unleashed
        ↓
Protagonist systematically confronts those responsible
        ↓
Entire hidden network mobilizes against him
        ↓
An ally reconnects protagonist to his true motive
        ↓
Final confrontation with the architects of the harm
        ↓
Debt is settled, but nothing is truly restored
        ↓
Protagonist chooses, in a small way, to continue living
